source: Davey, Gordon, Holland, Rutten & Williams, Bayesian Methods in the Search for MH370 (Springer, 2016). Page numbers are PDF pages of .sources/davey-2016/paper.pdf (124 pp.).
note: Every row states the published value or choice, where it comes from, and the dotted path at which this run's value is recorded in run.json. report/parameters.py joins the two and marks each row same / differs / not-in-book. Rows marked compare='declared' are prose or identifier choices where a string match is not a verdict; their 'status' is asserted here and explained in 'note'.

rows.label: Mach after an acceleration, uniform on
rows.note: Chosen for endurance, not measured: Assumption 7 (p. 73) and Assumption 4 (p. 73) make the floor a stand-in for the fuel constraint.

rows.label: Altitude after a vertical manoeuvre, uniform on
Vertical rate during a climb or descent
Manoeuvre integration step
rows.note: Known departure. At 500 kt and 15 deg bank a 5 s step turns 3 deg; the chord-versus-arc error over a 90 deg turn is of order 0.1 NM against a 29 us BTO sigma of about 2.3 NM.

rows.label: Position standard deviation
rows.cite: Table 8.2 (0.4 arcminutes in latitude and longitude)
rows.note: Known departure, slightly wider.

rows.label: Initial Mach set point
rows.note: Known departure: the base run draws the initial Mach uniformly on mach_range instead. The book's uniform 0.73-0.84 applies to Mach *after an acceleration* (p. 62), not to initialisation. Tested as hypotheses/initial-mach: shoulder 3.5% either way, not supported.

rows.label: Prior mean position and track
rows.note: Reconstructed here from the book's radar figures (5.624829 N, 99.048157 E, track 295.66 deg), because the book gives them only graphically.

rows.label: Autopilot-mode prior weights
rows.note: The book carries the mode as a state element fixed per particle; here each mode is a separate filter with an equal prior, combined by marginal likelihood.

rows.label: BTO fixed offset
rows.cite: p. 39 (T_nom 499,962 us; T_channel for R1200 -4,283 us)
rows.note: Eq. 5.3 read literally gives 504,245 us; 495,679 us is the combination that reproduces logged BTOs at known positions and matches Ashton et al. (2015).

rows.label: BTO noise sd, R1200
rows.note: Per-epoch, in data/satcom-observations.csv;

rows.label: BTO noise sd, anomalous R1200
rows.note: The book assigns BTO noise by message type. The two anomalous R1200 log-on acknowledges (18:25 and 00:19:37) are treated as their own class because their raw BTOs are known to be offset; the engine reads 43 us for them from the observations file. Run bto-29us collapses all three classes to the single R1200 value and changes the shoulder by 0.0005, so the class distinction is a fidelity choice rather than a modelling requirement.

rows.label: BTO noise sd, R600
rows.note: Known departure: this run assigns 63 us to the single 00:19:29 R600 log-on request; the book gives 62 us (p. 40).

rows.label: BFO noise sd
rows.note: This project's own successive-difference study puts the fast random component near 0.995 Hz (95% 0.859-1.183); the base run keeps the published 7 Hz so the reproduction stays comparable.

rows.label: BFO bias treatment
rows.note: Both treat the BFO bias as one unknown constant per trajectory and integrate it out in closed form rather than sampling it, so there is no numerical value to compare; the agreement is in the treatment.

rows.label: BTO bias treatment
rows.book: fixed per-flight T_channel only; no bias state
rows.note: Same here. The book records that T_channel is not stationary (Fig. 5.2 residual mean 10 us; Fig. 5.3 drift across 20 flights) and Assumption 2 (p. 73) names BTO variance inflation as a knob. Neither is tested in this project.

rows.label: Vertical rate in the BFO model
rows.note: Same here. 'The vertical rate will affect a BFO measurement but since the model only uses a nominal vertical rate it is unlikely to match any actual vertical manoeuvre in detail.' A descending particle is therefore scored with a level-flight BFO.

rows.label: 00:19 BFO
rows.note: Same here: the 00:19 BFOs are excluded from the cruise likelihood and reserved for the end-of-flight stage.

rows.label: Weather source
rows.note: Known departure: ERA5 here, 0.5 deg, hourly, 12 pressure altitudes from 500 to 43,000 ft. ACCESS-G is not public. Global RMS differences between ERA5, NCEP FNL and MERRA-2 are 2-2.4 m/s, below the model's own 5.68 kn wind-error sd.

rows.label: Magnetic declination source
rows.note: Known departure: IGRF-14 here.

rows.label: Resampling scheme
rows.book: randomised branching: weight >= eta branches n-bar times at w/n-bar; weight < eta branches once with probability w and is promoted to weight 1, else pruned. n-bar 3-10, eta e^-25 or e^-30, weights unnormalised until the end.
rows.note: Major departure, and the leading candidate for the missing northern shoulder. See results/shoulder-comparison.md sec. 5.

rows.label: Manoeuvre-type dependence
rows.book: turns, accelerations and vertical manoeuvres independent, sharing one time constant
rows.note: Same here. The book notes simultaneous changes are 'not precluded but not favoured', so coordinated manoeuvre sequences carry the product of three independent coincidences.

rows.label: Turn extent
rows.note: Same here. Turns are undirected, so goal-directed manoeuvre sequences are not favoured.

rows.label: Cost-index speed mode
rows.book: implemented but unused in most experiments; narrows the pdf slightly
rows.note: Known departure: omitted here (proprietary Boeing tables).

rows.label: Fuel and endurance
rows.book: infinite fuel; constraints applied to the pdf afterwards; fuel informs the Mach range
rows.note: Same here: no fuel state (fuel_kg is NaN). Any run that widens mach_range therefore removes the only endurance constraint in the model.

rows.label: Observation cutoff
rows.note: Both stop at the 00:19 log-on and use its BTO but not its BFO, the BFO being recorded during SDU start-up. A string match is not meaningful for a cutoff stated as a time and an exclusion.
